title: Requests and the supporting side
intro: This round is about requests to the Responsible Department: how they go out, how supporting doctors answer, reminders, re-fetch and outside reports. It ends with the demo PACS and hospital system the supporting side needs.

questions.question: When a required record was never ordered in the hospital system (no CT order at all), what should Vaidyx suggest?

options.label: Tell the doctor to order (Recommended)
options.description: The row says 'not ordered: place the order in the HIS'; requests go only to departments holding an order (pending, preliminary, unsigned). Vaidyx never places orders.

options.label: Request the department anyway
options.description: As today: a suggested request to Radiology, who must arrange the test with the treating team.

options.label: Order reminder and heads-up
options.description: The doctor is told to order it and the department gets an advance note.

questions.why: Today every gap becomes a suggested request to the Responsible Department; the accession and stage (ordered, scheduled, sample collected, cancelled) appear only when an order exists (V2 Phase 3). In the Indian HIS flow a report follows an order from the treating side (B1, docs_Eswar/research/indian_his.md). Vaidyx only reads the HIS.

questions.question: How should the suggested requests go out once the check has listed them?

options.label: One tap sends all (Recommended)
options.description: The doctor sees every suggested request with its draft, may edit or untick any, and sends them together; nothing goes without that tap.

options.label: One by one, as today
options.description: Each 'Notify <department>' is opened, edited and sent separately.

options.label: Automatic unless held
options.description: Requests go out by themselves after a set time (for example 2 hours) unless the doctor holds them.

questions.why: V2 4.2: the check only suggests; the doctor edits and sends each one, in-app or 'Open in mail'; nothing automatic. J1: one Notify dialog per gap. The owner wants few clicks; R01 decides what the AI may do without a click ('expert over the loop').
questions.skip_if: Skip if R01-Q02 answered 'Everything, including sending' or 'Sends after a hold' (sending is then automatic).

questions.question: Through which channels should a request reach the supporting department?

options.label: In-app inbox (Recommended)
options.description: Always on; the department sees the request with UHID, IP / OP No. and accession in Vaidyx.

options.label: Email sent by Vaidyx
options.description: Vaidyx sends the mail itself through a hospital mail server, instead of today's draft in the doctor's own mail app.

options.label: WhatsApp or SMS alert
options.description: A short alert with no patient name and a link into Vaidyx; needs a paid business gateway and the hospital's consent rules.

options.label: Phone call button
options.description: On a phone, one tap opens the dialer with the department's number, like the board members' call option.

questions.why: Today: in-app plus a mailto draft or Copy draft; the server sends no email (V2 §3, §13). Settled: calls open the phone's dialer for board members. Unverified in research: whether Indian boards share cases on WhatsApp (data.js research.unverified). R14 sets channels for all other notifications; R15 sets patient data on phones.

questions.question: Should a request go to the department as a whole or to a named doctor?

options.label: Department, first to take (Recommended)
options.description: Any doctor of the department takes it; the others see who has it, so nothing waits on one person on leave.

options.label: Named doctor
options.description: The treating doctor picks a person, for example the radiologist who reported the scan; the rest of the department sees it read-only.

options.label: Head assigns it
options.description: The department head receives it and passes it to a doctor; one more step, clear ownership.

questions.why: Today requests reach the department inbox and any member acknowledges (B7, matrix answer_request). Signed reports name their signer ('Digitally signed by Dr X', V2 §3), so the reporting doctor is known. I12 phone-first supporting views liked. R02 defines what 'head' means.

questions.question: Should Vaidyx re-fetch records from the hospital system by itself?

options.label: On Done, plus half-hourly (Recommended)
options.description: Re-fetches when a department sends Done and every 30 minutes for Case Files with open requests; requests close when the signed report arrives, even with no Done.

options.label: Only when Done is sent
options.description: One automatic re-fetch per Done; a report signed without a Done waits for a manual re-fetch.

options.label: Manual, one tap in notice
options.description: The doctor taps 'Re-fetch now' in the Done notification (I15); nothing runs by itself.

questions.why: G21: re-fetch is manual only, so the owner must remember it. I15 (one-tap re-fetch from the notification) liked ('i15 is okay'). Re-fetch pulls only changed versions and re-runs the check in milliseconds (B8). Background polling was out of scope for V2 (changes_v2 §13).

questions.question: What must a supporting doctor do inside Vaidyx for each request?

options.label: Nothing required, Done optional (Recommended)
options.description: They sign in their own RIS / LIS / PACS as usual; the request closes when the signed report arrives. Take up and Done with a note stay optional.

options.label: Take up and Done
options.description: As today: two taps in Vaidyx plus signing in their own system; the owner sees each step.

options.label: Done only
options.description: One tap after signing; no take-up step.

questions.why: Eswar 13 Oct: 'a radiologist won't upload anything ... our platform is a notification carrier'. G20: two systems; J2 friction: 'the request looks open until someone else acts'. The first option needs automatic re-fetch (R08-Q05).

questions.question: Can a supporting department send a request back to the treating doctor?

options.label: Yes, with a reason list (Recommended)
options.description: Reasons such as 'wrong department', 'no order in the HIS', 'patient must come', 'already reported'; the owner is told and can re-send elsewhere.

options.label: Yes, free text only
options.description: Any reason typed; harder to count on the quality dashboard.

options.label: No, as today
options.description: They can only acknowledge or send Done; a wrong request waits until the owner closes it.

questions.why: dept_requests.py has acknowledge, done, remind and close by the owner, but no return. A request reaching the wrong desk (route overrides V2 2.4, G12) has no way back today.

questions.question: Should overdue requests send reminders by themselves?

options.label: Due day, then daily (Recommended)
options.description: The department is reminded on the due date and each working day after; the owner's list shows 'overdue'.

options.label: Once, when overdue
options.description: One automatic reminder the day after the due date; any more by hand.

options.label: Manual only, as today
options.description: Only the owner's team or the coordinator presses Remind.

questions.why: K09: overdue never notifies; it is worked out only when a page is shown. I13 proposed overdue reminders and digests; U17: the coordinator had 536 unread notifications, so R14 groups them. Due dates today: the record's days from sending (CBC 2, molecular 10), calendar days.

questions.question: When a request stays overdue, who should be told next?

options.label: Head, then coordinator (Recommended)
options.description: After 2 working days overdue the supporting department's head is told, and it shows on the coordinator's chase list for the board date.

options.label: Coordinator only
options.description: Overdue requests go on the coordinator's chase list; the coordinator chases by phone or Remind.

options.label: No escalation
options.description: Only the reminders chosen above; the owner decides what to do.

questions.why: Today the coordinator reminds on the owner's behalf (B15, Remind / Remind owner); nothing escalates. R02 defines 'head of department'; R10 covers the coordinator's chasing before the agenda.

questions.question: When the treating doctor asks a radiologist or pathologist to confirm a report before the board, what do they give back?

options.label: Report stands or addendum (Recommended)
options.description: One tap, 'Report stands' or 'Addendum pending', with an optional note; the board sees it with their name and time.

options.label: Plus a comment for board
options.description: They may also type or speak a short comment in their own words, shown to the board as theirs.

options.label: Plus review of AI brief
options.description: They also mark their specialty's AI brief reviewed or flagged (see R09).

questions.why: I08 liked, 'specially requested from the treatment doctor' (notes, role-supporting). ICMR-NCDIR survey: radiologists attend 46.7% and pathologists 28.5% of Indian boards, so an answer before the meeting helps. Vaidyx records their words; it never writes an opinion for them.

questions.question: Can a report from another hospital or private lab meet a required record?

options.label: Yes, after doctor attests (Recommended)
options.description: Counts once the treating doctor attests it final; labelled 'outside report' everywhere, including the summary and the room.

options.label: Pathology needs in-house review
options.description: Outside histopathology counts only with this hospital's Pathology review report; other outside reports count after attest.

options.label: Same rules as today
options.description: Counts when its text shows final and a signature line (Sd/-), like any report; attest only when both are missing.

questions.why: B9 / V2 3.6: the treating doctor uploads outside reports; they are read, labelled and patient-matched, and a name-only match counts only after the doctor confirms. Validation sheet check 3: uploads need a signature line or Sd/-. Patients visit 2 to 3 hospitals per episode (data.js patient role).

questions.question: Which open-source base should the demo PACS and hospital system for supporting doctors use?

options.label: Extend our own mock (Recommended)
options.description: Add a worklist and 'sign' screen for radiologists and pathologists to the e-Hospital-style mock HIS, keep Orthanc + OHIF; synthetic, localhost, quickest.

options.label: Bahmni
options.description: India-built system (OpenMRS, OpenELIS lab, PACS link, ABDM ready); realistic, but heavy and usually installed with Docker, not allowed on this server.

options.label: OpenMRS 3 with radiology
options.description: OpenMRS plus its radiology module sending HL7 orders to Orthanc; lighter than Bahmni, more set-up than our mock.

options.label: GNU Health
options.description: Hospital-wide open-source system with lab and imaging; less India-specific, limited FHIR.

questions.why: Settled: supporting doctors need a demo PACS and HIS, built later (notes role-supporting). Held: his_mock (FHIR R4 NRCeS, RIS / LIS desk 'Complete and sign') and Orthanc + OHIF (CLAUDE.md: no Docker, no sudo). NIC e-Hospital is a government cloud service (SaaS), not downloadable, so only its style can be copied. Web check 17 Oct: Bahmni wiki (pacs-integration with dcm4chee, Bahmni Lite, ABDM), OpenMRS radiology module (HL7 ORM to any PACS), Orthanc worklists plugin, openIMIS EMR benchmark (GNU Health FHIR limited), informatics.nic.in e-Hospital brochure.

questions.question: When should the demo PACS and hospital system for supporting doctors be built?

options.label: With supporting doctor screens (Recommended)
options.description: Built in the same step as the new phone-first supporting views (T17), so the whole request loop can be shown.

options.label: Before the UI rebuild
options.description: Built first, so every new screen is designed against it; the rebuild starts later.

options.label: After all role screens
options.description: The supporting side is shown with today's mock desk until the end.

questions.why: T17 (supporting doctor: phone first) kept; I12 and I14 liked. R16 sets the overall build order and demo dates; this only places the demo systems.

questions.question: Can you find out which HIS, RIS, LIS and PACS the doctors' hospital uses, with any interface notes?

options.label: I'll ask the hospital (Recommended)
options.description: The demo copies the order and words of their screens, and we learn whether a deep link to an order (I14) is possible.

options.label: Skip for now
options.description: The demo follows the generic e-Hospital style; deep links work only in our mock.

options.label: Use e-Hospital public documents
options.description: We model the demo on NIC e-Hospital's published module list (registration, OPD, IPD, LIS, RIS).

questions.why: changes_v2 §12 lists 'the hospital's real HIS / PACS vendor and interface notes, from the hospital IT team' as still to obtain. I14 (deep link to the department's own system) liked; it needs the vendor's link format.

resource.item: Names and versions of the hospital's HIS, RIS, LIS and PACS, and any interface notes (FHIR or HL7 endpoints, the link format that opens an order or a study)
resource.source_url: No public URL: the hospital IT team, through Dr Minmini (Radiology) or Dr Usha (Biochemistry); fallback https://informatics.nic.in/uploads/pdfs/4d85cc7c_04_11_ehospital_suite_folder_new.pdf
resource.why: Makes the demo look like the systems the supporting doctors use and tells us if I14 deep links are possible.
